newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico says seven ports closed for Storm Hernan.
newsitem.headline: Mexico says seven ports closed for Storm Hernan.

text.p: Mexico has now closed seven ports because of the threat posed by Tropical Storm Hernan, the Communications and Transportation Ministry said Tuesday.

Six ports are on the Pacific coast and one, namely Coatzacoalcos in the state of Veracruz, is on the Gulf of Mexico, the ministry said. The ministry reported Monday that three ports were closed for the threatening storm.
The Pacific Coast ports closed are Manzanillo in Colima state, Acapulco and Zihuatanejo in Guerrero, Salina Cruz and Puerto Angel in Oaxaca and Puerto Madero in Chiapas state.

Hernan is around 445 km (278 miles) south-southwest of the port of Zihuatanejo, with sustained winds of 65 km per hour (41 mph) and gusts of 85 km per hour (53 mph), the ministry said. "It is expected to gain force in the next 24 hours," it added.

Several ports that were closed Monday to small vessels, fishing and tourist boats, were re-opened Tuesday. The ports were Tecolutla, Nautla, Veracruz, Alvarado and Tlacotalpan in the state of Veracruz.
